b.x: This does not teach a weapon, a fight, a militia, a break-in, or flight from authority. Army technique, here, is what fits a civilian: see, stop, decide, do not lie to yourself. The body now: the red page, 192. This page does not dial.
Whoever arrives now

You do not need the film. You need an order. The prepared gray man is not the one who adds equipment. He is the one who still chooses when the street, the house, and the head tighten at the same time. This protocol is the door. What comes after, on the channel, is water, food, fire, shelter, aid, and the mind. Here is what ties it: knowing your own error before the day, reading the place by the one thing that does not belong, reading the person by what they ask you to do, and acting in a step that was already chosen. No audience. No sentence of the one who waits to be sure.
The three lines, written cold

Operational self-knowledge is not a pretty sentence. It is three lines, on paper, made on a calm Tuesday. The first: your tell. What your body does when fear rises. The hand in the pocket, the voice that speeds up, the laugh, the step that locks. Whoever does not name the tell thinks he is calm when he has already given himself away. The second: the lie you tell yourself. The sentence you use in order to stay. It will pass. It is nothing. I can handle it. That sentence is the delay. The third: your stupid hour. The hour of the day, or the night without sleep, when your decision gets worse. Write it. In the chaos you will not discover it. You will repeat it. The army calls it knowing yourself before the mission. In civilian life it is the same fact: the person who did not measure himself in the easy measures himself in the worst, and loses.
Live in the yellow

There is an old code, from people who teach how not to be caught by surprise. It serves here, without the weapon. White: you are inside your own head. The place does not exist. That is how the street chooses. Yellow: you are present, without a story. You see the door, the line, the exit, who changed course. It is not tension. It is the normal mode of someone who intends to come home. Orange: one specific thing went wrong. Then attention narrows to it, not to the whole world. Red: the act, short, and the return to yellow. The error of chaos is to live in the red the whole month. Red spends sleep, speech, and the family. The prepared gray man lives in the yellow. He visits the orange. He does not camp in the red.
One thing that does not belong

Analyzing what is wrong is not scanning the whole scene. The whole scan tires you and does not see. The method is the baseline. How this place is when it is ordinary: the noise, the pace, who works, who passes. You keep that in the yellow, without effort, because you pass there always. The wrong thing is one break only. The shop open with the light off. The man standing who is not waiting for a bus. The silence on a street that never goes silent. Two people who do not look at each other and walk in the same step. One is enough. Two, you change course. You do not stay to complete the picture. The complete picture is the luxury of whoever is already in the middle.
The mind shows up in the request

Reading a person is not a catalog of the face. The face lies, and so does yours. What does not lie easily is the request. What this person needs you to do in the next ten seconds. Stop. Come along. Look the other way. Open the door. Say you are alone. Take out the phone. Confirm the way. The mind, in chaos, shows up there: in the verb they want from you. If the verb isolates you, delays you, or takes you out of the light, you have already read it. You do not need the story that comes with it. Good people ask too. The difference is the cost. A good request survives a no. A request that closes in when you refuse was not a request. It was a test. Emotional intelligence, at this degree, is not explaining the no. It is seeing the verb, paying the cost of seeming rude, and going on.
The loop: see, orient, choose, act

A pilot described what decides a short encounter. It is not speed of hand. It is a loop. See what is there. Orient: what that means for you, now, with what you already know of yourself. Choose. Act. And see again, because the place changed with your act. People lose at orient. They see the fact and orient it inside the film: it is the end, it is war, it is nothing. Both errors. To orient is to put the fact in your real life. I have an exit. I have the children. I have water for today. This request isolates me. Then the choice is small. It is not the month's plan. It is the next step. Acting without orienting is panic. Orienting without acting is the lie of the second line. The loop only closes if all four happen, fast, and again.
Twenty seconds, stopped

When the group stops, in the brush or on the building stairs, twenty seconds without talking. Ear. What changed in the noise. Eye. The exit, the person, the water. Nose. Smoke, sewage, gas. That is a field halt, taught to people who walk on a mission, and it serves the family with no uniform at all. Only then the order of work, and the order is not negotiated. First the safety of the place: the door, the wind, what can fall. Then the water. Then the food. Then the hygiene. Last, the rest. Whoever eats first and looks after eats in the wrong place. Whoever talks during the twenty seconds hears their own theory. In the chaos, the theory is what was already wrong before you stopped.
When the body locks

Locking is not cowardice. It is a state of the body, fast, before the sentence. Fight, flee, or go still. All three are old. The gray man does not wait for the inner speech to unlock. He has one small act already chosen, rehearsed in the easy. Three long exhales. One step toward the light. The hand on the child. The one-word sentence: no. The act does not solve the chaos. It gives the loop back. Without a pre-chosen act, white becomes red without passing through yellow, and the family sees a stopped man thinking he is thinking. He is not thinking. He is absent. The rehearsal is on Tuesday, with a quiet heart. In the fright, the body only delivers what it repeated.
What breaks first

In the extreme state, the city fails slowly. The person fails first. First, sleep. Without sleep, yellow becomes white and the tell grows. Sleep in turns if there are two adults. One listens. The other really sleeps. Not both in a watch of pride. Then speech. Whoever narrates the fear out loud hands the verb to the whole house, and the children keep it. Speak the next step, not the film. Then pride. The need to be right in the hall, to show the stock, to go back to the dangerous place so you do not seem to have stepped back. Stepping back early is the technique. Staying to prove it is the man who did not write the second line. The food ends on the day the count says. The person ends on the night he did not sleep and still wanted to win the conversation.
What this protocol closes

Three lines on paper. Yellow as home. One break, not the whole picture. The verb of the request. The loop, again. Twenty seconds quiet. One small act already rehearsed. Sleep before pride. That is the fully prepared gray man in what depends on him. The rest is tool and it is on the channel: the count, the water, the fire outside, the shelter, the aid. It is not a troop legend. It is what the troop teaches and the civilian can use without becoming a troop. If someone's body has failed now, leave this page. The red one is above. 192.
